prompt: Boss. Found a tiny wood box. Make plink-plink noises when I spin the handle. Make it stop, or I eat it.

dialogues.text: Sound like a sad elf. Very annoying.
It make Gribble cry. So yes, evil magic.

prompt: Master! The stars say today is a bad day for the Swarm! We must hide under the floorboards until tomorrow!

dialogues.btn: Who taught you to read stars?
dialogues.text: We ate a wizard's eyeball! Now we knows things!

dialogues.btn: What exactly did the stars say?
dialogues.text: The big shiny dot winked! It means certain doom!

prompt: Overlord. I propose we send 'formal declarations of war' to the human villages before we burn them. The terror of anticipation is exquisite.

dialogues.btn: Won't that give them time to prepare?
dialogues.text: Yes. It makes the slaughter slightly less boring.
'You are cordially invited to your own disembowelment.' I used a very nice wax seal.

prompt: Caught a humie [[Painted Demon]]. He honked at me with demonic nose! Chop da skull-crushing shoes?!

dialogues.text: Yes! He wears paints of a demon leer! And massive shoes for crushing skulls!

dialogues.btn: Is his honk a war cry?
dialogues.text: It freeze Kargoth in his tracks! Very strong magic honk!

prompt: Boss... the lower levels are flooding with blood. Again. Do we drain it, or just buy taller boots? I am tired of draining it.

dialogues.text: I stopped keeping track three centuries ago, Boss.
They float. Mostly.

prompt: Overlord. The Deep Flame demands a theatrical tragedy. Shall we force the goblins to act out 'Hamlet', or just set them on fire?

dialogues.text: They believe it is a play about a small, delicious pig. It is a disaster.
Fire always appeases the Flame, Overlord. It is wonderfully predictable.

prompt: My Lord. I have decided to take a goblin squire. His name is 'Mud'. I shall teach him the heavy, depressing burden of chivalry.

dialogues.text: He looked at a puddle with the same profound despair I feel looking at the stars.
His bones are brittle, but his spirit is appropriately shattered.

prompt: Overlord! I've started selling 'I Survived [[The Iron Pits]]' shrouds to fleeing heroes! The profit margins are incredible!

dialogues.text: No, no! It's very cheap cotton. It offers negative armor class!
They get a 5% royalty on every hero they deliberately let escape.

nextCard.cardText: Overlord! The surface-dwellers are treating our death-traps like an amusement park! They are lining up outside for the 'Lava Flume Ride'!

prompt: OVERLORD. GRAVITY IS BECOMING TEDIOUS. MAY I INVERT IT IN THE EAST WING FOR MY AMUSEMENT?

dialogues.btn: What happens to the Orcs there?
dialogues.text: THEY WILL LEARN TO WALK ON THE CEILING. OR THEY WILL FALL UPWARDS FOREVER.
GOLD IS HEAVY. IT WILL MAKE A DELIGHTFUL, LETHAL RAIN.

prompt: OVERLORD. THESE INTERMINABLE SWIPES DEMAND A FINAL CHOICE. ==THE UNPAID DEVELOPER== APPEARS! ACCEPTS HIS OFFER?

dialogues.text: A DIVINE ENTITY THAT DEMANDS TITHES OF 'COFFEE' TO DESIGN THIS VERY REALITY.
A CONCEPT CALLED 'PAID LEAVE'. WHERE HE STOPS WATCHING YOUR STRUGGLES.
